Date: 2026-03-27

Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Anita Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO - Springfield Care), Evan Cho (VP Eng), Lisa Brenner (Head MLOps)
summary: Redwood walked Springfield Care through the Model Catalog: selecting open models, benchmark comparisons, and compatibility matrices for hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Customer expressed interest in a Dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost with their sample workload; security and VPC/KMS were called out as gating items.
topics: Model selection (open models vs tuned variants)
Benchmark interpretation (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per token)
Compatibility matrices (quantization, GPU types, sequence length limits)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, with Anita our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marta: Good, thanks, excited to see the model catalog walkthrough. We're evaluating options for our triage assistant and patient messaging workloads.
[00:15] Anita: Great, we'll focus first on how to pick open models from our catalog, then how to read the benchmark sheets, and finally the compatibility matrix so you can see what runs on Dedicated vs Private.
[00:28] Evan: Quick ask before we start - our main concern is p95 latency under 300ms for the triage use case, cost ideally not to exceed current token budget.
[00:36] Jordan: Totally, we'll call those out. Anita, slide into the model catalog?
[00:40] Anita: Yep, pulling up the model catalog - bear with me, screen is a bit slow. So here you can filter by task, e.g., chat, generation, embeddings. We curate open models and show a performance profile - measured median latency, p95, throughput on different GPUs, and recommended quantization.
[00:56] Marta: Are these benchmarks from Redwood infra or public numbers? Sometimes open model pages have different numbers.
[01:02] Anita: Good question. These are Redwood-run benchmarks on our standard inference runtime; we test across a few representative sequence lengths and batch sizes. There's a raw spreadsheet linked per-model (we'll send the sheet). Note: transcripts sometimes flip model names, our test suite uses canonical repo tags but the UI uses shorter names.
[01:18] Evan: When you say "recommend quantization" what does that mean exactly? Like int8 vs int4 and the tradeoffs?
[01:24] Anita: Exactly. The catalog shows quantization profiles we validated - int8 is often a good latency/cost balance with minor quality delta, int4 gives better cost but can impact some generation coherency. We also flag models that are quantization-friendly vs those that need FP16. The compatibility matrix indicates which GPU types and whether KV cache sharing is supported.
[01:40] Lisa: For our POC we'll likely want a dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbors and get predictable p95. Can Redwood do dedicated with our VPC?
[01:48] Jordan: Yes - Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and we can set up VPC peering or Private deployment depending on your compliance needs. For SOC 2/hipaa-heavy customers we recommend Private with a customer-managed control plane.
[02:00] Marta: We are HIPAA-adjacent, need audit logs and KMS. How do you expose keys?
[02:05] Anita: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS/HSM) in Private; Dedicated can also use envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or customer keys for higher assurance. We'll share our security pack.
[02:15] Evan: Back to the benchmarks - can you show an example for a 2k token response? Our triage completions often hit 1.5-2k tokens.
[02:22] Anita: Yep, switching to the benchmark sheet. For a 2k sequence, Model A (open) shows p50 85ms, p95 270ms on A100-80GB with int8; throughput about 80 req/s with batching. Model B (smaller) hits p95 ~340ms so it might miss your 300ms SLO at peak. There's also a cost-per-1k-token estimate.
[02:40] Marta: The 270ms p95 looks promising. How reliable are these numbers vs real traffic?
[02:45] Anita: They're representative but depend on your arrival pattern. We recommend a short dedicated benchmark using your sample traces to validate. Redwood Optimize will also recommend batching windows and cache hints to reduce tail latency.
[02:58] Evan: Does KV cache work across sessions? For chat continuity we need prefix caching, and frequent context reuse.
[03:04] Anita: We support KV caching; the catalog notes which models and runtime builds enable shared KV cache and prefix caching. On Dedicated we can enable persistent KV shards for longer context windows. That reduces compute for repeated prefixes and helps latency.
[03:18] Lisa: Any gotchas with long sequences and quantization? We've seen hallucinations increase when aggressive quantization is applied on some models.
[03:25] Anita: Yes, that's why the catalog flags models with known sensitivity to low-bit quantization. For triage where accuracy matters, we'd start at int8 and evaluate quality using your eval prompts. Redwood Optimize can run regression checks against your prompt set.
[03:37] Jordan: Quick interjection - pricing note: Hosted lowest friction but per-token costs are higher. Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing which lowers unit cost; Private adds platform/ops fees but is required for stricter compliance. We'll include rough numbers in the deck.
[03:50] Marta: For the compatibility matrix, can we get a CSV with which models run on our preferred GPU stack (we use T4s + a couple of A10s)?
[03:58] Anita: Absolutely. The compatibility matrix export includes GPU compatibility, quantization support, max sequence length, and kernel caveats. We'll export and send.
[04:07] Evan: How does routing/fallback work if a model variant isn't available? We want graceful degradation rather than errors.
[04:13] Anita: Smart routing can fall back to a compatible variant; for example if a low-latency int8 variant isn't available, we can fallback to a slightly larger FP16 model with a retry policy, or route to hosted as an escape hatch. Policies are configurable per-route.
[04:25] Marta: Any notes about multi-region? We'd like US-East primary and US-West DR.
[04:30] Jordan: You can pin region priorities; the catalog indicates regional availability per image. We'll show a sample routing policy for US-East primary with US-West failover.
[04:38] Evan: Security again - audit logs retention? We need 365 days for certain events, or at least an export path.
[04:44] Anita: Audit logs are supported and can stream to your SIEM. Retention tiers are an add-on but we can export daily. We'll include the security addendum.
[04:52] Marta: Great. Can we run a short benchmark with 1 hour of our traffic profile on Dedicated? We want p95 numbers and token cost.
[04:59] Jordan: Yes, Anita will coordinate. We'll need sample traces and expected concurrency.
[05:05] Anita: I'll send a sample benchmark plan. For the POC we'd recommend 1-2 instance types (A10 and A100) and the candidate models from the catalog. We'll capture p50/p95, token cost, and quality regressions.
[05:18] Lisa: One more: can Redwood help with rollout strategies? We want canary then gradual ramp and automatic fallback.
[05:24] Jordan: Redwood Console supports canary, A/B, automatic fallback, and traffic shaping. We can define success metrics (latency/noise/errors) to auto-roll back.
[05:33] Evan: Ok sounds good. Next steps?
[05:36] Jordan: Recap - I'll send the model catalog deck, benchmark spreadsheet, and compatibility matrix export. Anita will propose a benchmark plan and calendar invite for the Dedicated run. Marta, you'll share sample payloads and acceptance criteria. We'll reconvene after initial benchmark.
[05:49] Marta: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:51] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:52] (call ends)
